clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) (held current text, authority of the subsection may be transferred by the President to the Secretary of State) and Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b) (held as a savings note under 3056A: the title does not affect any Executive order transferring to the Secretary of State the authority of 3 U.S.C. 208 in effect on the day before the effective date of that Act); the held U.S. Code note prints this order after the recodification; bounded searches name no ending.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 transfers to the Secretary of State the authority to determine the need for and approve the terms of reimbursable extraordinary protective activities for foreign diplomatic missions (former 3 U.S.C. 202(7), now 18 U.S.C. 3056A(a)(7)) and the authority to reimburse State and local governments (former 3 U.S.C. 208(a), now 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d)). The former sections were repealed and recodified in 2006, but Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b) preserved an Executive order transferring the section 208 authority to the Secretary of State, and 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) itself provides that the authority of that subsection may be transferred by the President to the Secretary of State.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing effect of the transfer, as for section 1: the held U.S. Code note under 18 U.S.C. 3056A prints section 2 as current text; no held instrument revokes or reverses it, and the bounded searches name no ending.
clauses.reason: Operative as a completed transfer whose effect persists. Section 2 transferred to the Secretary of State such unexpended moneys as had been appropriated to the Department of the Treasury for reimbursements under former 3 U.S.C. 208(a); the transfer took effect with the order on October 1, 1984 (section 4), and no held instrument reverses it. Whether any moneys remained to transfer is not held, and the clause is carried on the reading that the order's self-executing allocation stands.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) (held current text) links the Secretary of State's duties under paragraphs (7) and (9) to authority under the Foreign Missions Act, and the held References in Text note places that Act at 22 U.S.C. 4301 et seq.; the held U.S. Code note prints section 3 as current text.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 3 requires the transferred authority to be exercised in coordination with the protective security programs the Secretary of State administers under the Foreign Missions Act of 1982 and allows authority under that Act to be applied to any mission covered by the former section 202(7). The Foreign Missions Act is still classified at 22 U.S.C. 4301 et seq. (held 3056A text, references in text), and 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) now says the Secretary of State may use authority under title II of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 in carrying out the paragraph (7) and (9) duties.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: the order took effect on October 1, 1984 by its own terms and has not been revoked; the held U.S. Code note under 18 U.S.C. 3056A prints it, and Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b) treated a transfer order in effect on March 8, 2006 as continuing.
clauses.reason: Operative as the effective-date clause of an order still in force. Section 4 fixed October 1, 1984 as the date the order took effect; that date has passed and was the start of the order's effect, not an end, and no source shows any later instrument changing it. It is recorded as operative because the order's effectiveness from that date is what sections 1 to 3 rest on.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (49 FR 22053, PDF page 23) is Executive Order 12478 of May 23, 1984, Ronald Reagan, Transfer of Authority to the Secretary of State To Make Reimbursements for Protection of Foreign Missions to International Organizations; the four inventory clauses are sections 1 to 4 (section 4 is effective on October 1, 1984). Current law: the authority transferred came from former 3 U.S.C. 202(7) and 208(a), recodified by Pub. L. 109-177 title VI section 605(a) (March 9, 2006) at 18 U.S.C. 3056A(a)(7) and (d); the held text of 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) says the authority of that subsection may be transferred by the President to the Secretary of State and that in carrying out duties under paragraphs (7) and (9) the Secretary of State may use authority under title II of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (Foreign Missions Act), and the held savings provision, Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b), says that title does not affect any Executive order transferring to the Secretary of State the authority of section 208 of title 3 in effect on the day before March 9, 2006. The held U.S. Code note under 18 U.S.C. 3056A prints this order with the former section numbers marked, and no ending. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order.
